random_library_passage.selection_procedure: Curated six non-personal research PDFs from the user's Trading library in the explicit order below; Python random.Random(20261018).randrange(6) selects the document, then the next randrange(1, 11) selects a PDF page after confirming the selected PDF has 10 pages.
random_library_passage.actual_short_passage: Because the losses associated with underestimating PIN are so much greater than the potential profit when it is correctly estimated
random_library_passage.use_and_limit: This secondary market-education passage was used only as a low-weight analogy for shrinking a sequence gate toward a fixed blend when conditional expert quality is uncertain. Challenge 2 has a symmetric clipped weighted squared-error metric; no asymmetric market-risk behavior or PIN semantics are inferred.

sources.citation: Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan, and Hinton (1991), Adaptive Mixtures of Local Experts.
sources.official_code: No author-maintained implementation located during this search.
sources.source_component: Supervised gate assigning cases to specialist predictors.
sources.learned_objective_and_feedback: The abstract reports supervised learning on a vowel-discrimination task; labels and gate/expert training feedback are available in that task.
sources.transfer_boundary: Supports conditional routing as a mechanism, not Challenge 2 accuracy, sequence-level generalization, or test-time error access.

sources.citation: Adams and MacKay (2007), Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection, arXiv:0710.3742.
sources.source_component: Recursive posterior over run length from current observation likelihood and a change-point hazard.
sources.learned_objective_and_feedback: Unsupervised sequential observation likelihood; the algorithm consumes the observed stream and maintains run-length beliefs, without downstream target labels.
sources.transfer_boundary: Only the input-only innovation/run-length signal is proposed. No semantic event, instrument, venue, or target interpretation is made.

sources.citation: Oreshkin et al. (2019/2020), N-BEATS: Neural basis expansion analysis for interpretable time series forecasting, arXiv:1905.10437.
sources.source_component: Doubly residual backcast connection with partial forecasts accumulated across blocks.
sources.learned_objective_and_feedback: Supervised point forecasting on M3, M4, and Tourism data with true training targets and forecast evaluation.
sources.transfer_boundary: Multivariate anonymous indicators and the fixed weighted clip2 metric differ. The proposal transfers staged residual correction only. The code repository states CC BY-NC; no code is copied or executed.

sources.citation: Dong et al. (2023), SimMTM: A Simple Pre-Training Framework for Masked Time-Series Modeling, arXiv:2302.00861.
sources.source_component: Masked input reconstruction via aggregation of complementary masked views and time-series neighborhood structure.
sources.learned_objective_and_feedback: Self-supervised raw-series reconstruction during pretraining; downstream fine-tuning/evaluation uses forecasting/classification labels in reported benchmarks.
sources.transfer_boundary: Proposal uses only a fit-group causal reconstruction objective and discards decoder/retrieval at inference; it does not reproduce full SimMTM or transfer published benchmark gains.

sources.citation: Tallec and Ollivier (2018), Can recurrent neural networks warp time?, arXiv:1804.11188 / ICLR 2018.
sources.source_component: Gate-bias initialization encodes a spread of time constants for GRU/LSTM memory.
sources.learned_objective_and_feedback: Paper studies supervised sequence-prediction/long-delay and time-warping tasks with training/validation sequence feedback.
sources.transfer_boundary: Its tasks and sequence scales differ from Challenge 2; exact gate signs must follow the canonical model implementation, and no local gain is presumed.

sources.citation: Liu et al. (2025), Efficient Multivariate Time Series Forecasting via Calibrated Language Models with Privileged Knowledge Distillation, arXiv:2505.02138.
sources.source_component: Teacher-to-student transfer with prediction/correlation and feature discrepancy objectives.
sources.learned_objective_and_feedback: Reported forecasting uses dataset targets and teacher-generated information; the teacher receives future ground-truth prompts as privileged inputs, while evaluation scores forecasts against targets.
sources.transfer_boundary: Future prompts, external pretrained language models, external market data, and any future test input are excluded. Only offline prediction/feature distillation from a strictly causal last-60 input window is considered.

sources.citation: Izmailov et al. (2018), Averaging Weights Leads to Wider Optima and Better Generalization, arXiv:1803.05407.
sources.source_component: Average parameters sampled along one SGD trajectory under a constant or cyclical learning-rate schedule.
sources.learned_objective_and_feedback: Supervised cross-entropy training with labeled CIFAR/ImageNet evaluation in the paper; no downstream test labels are consumed by the averaging rule.
sources.transfer_boundary: Different architecture/task. Cheap only if compatible same-run snapshots already exist; unrelated seeds are not parameter-aligned.

sources.citation: Bandara et al. (2020), Improving the Accuracy of Global Forecasting Models using Time Series Data Augmentation, arXiv:2008.02663.
sources.official_code: No paper-author official repository verified in this search.
sources.source_component: GRATIS, moving-block bootstrap, and DTW barycentric averaging to augment series for global recurrent forecasting.
sources.learned_objective_and_feedback: Supervised forecast-window fitting and sMAPE/MASE-style evaluation on energy, NN3/NN5/AusGrid and related forecasting sets.
sources.transfer_boundary: Its series-generation assumptions and forecast metrics differ; independent perturbations of anonymous Challenge 2 channels are not supported by the paper.
